import Mathlib

set_option linter.unusedVariables false
set_option maxRecDepth 1000000
set_option maxHeartbeats 40000000

abbrev Grid := List (List Nat)
abbrev Cell := Nat × Nat

def cellAt (g : Grid) (y x : Nat) : Nat := (g.getD y []).getD x 0

def gridMap (g : Grid) (f : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat) : Grid :=
  (List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    (List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).map fun x => f y x (cellAt g y x)

def recolorMap (g : Grid) (m : List (Nat × Nat)) : Grid :=
  gridMap g fun _ _ c => ((m.find? (fun p => p.1 == c)).map Prod.snd).getD c

def consumeRowExtremal (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Grid :=
  g.map fun row =>
    let idxs := (List.range row.length).filter (fun x => row.getD x 0 == color)
    match (if useMin then idxs.head? else idxs.getLast?) with
    | none => row
    | some k => (List.range row.length).map fun x => if x = k then repl else row.getD x 0

def countColor (g : Grid) (c : Nat) : Nat :=
  (g.map (fun row => (row.filter (fun v => v == c)).length)).foldl (· + ·) 0

def consumeRowExtremalK (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Nat → Grid
  | 0 => g
  | Nat.succ k => consumeRowExtremalK (consumeRowExtremal g color repl useMin) color repl useMin k

def adj (a b : Cell) : Bool :=
  ((a.1 == b.1) && (a.2 + 1 == b.2 || b.2 + 1 == a.2)) ||
  ((a.2 == b.2) && (a.1 + 1 == b.1 || b.1 + 1 == a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ! comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

def component (seed : Cell) (cells : List Cell) (fuel : Nat) : List Cell :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => [seed]
  | Nat.succ f =>
    let rec go (n : Nat) (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell :=
      match n with
      | 0 => comp
      | Nat.succ m =>
        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2
    go (Nat.succ f) [seed] (cells.filter (fun c => c ≠ seed))

def matchCells (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List Cell :=
  ((List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    ((List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).filter
      (fun x => colors.contains (cellAt g y x))).map (fun x => (y, x))).flatten

def componentsOf (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List (List Cell) :=
  let cells := matchCells g colors
  let rec go (n : Nat) (remaining : List Cell) (acc : List (List Cell)) : List (List Cell) :=
    match n, remaining with
    | 0, _ => acc
    | _, [] => acc
    | Nat.succ m, seed :: _ =>
      let comp := component seed remaining remaining.length
      go m (remaining.filter (fun c => ! comp.contains c)) (acc ++ [comp])
  go cells.length cells []

def distinctColors (g : Grid) (comp : List Cell) : Nat :=
  (comp.map (fun c => cellAt g c.1 c.2)).eraseDups.length

def compOk (g : Grid) (comp : List Cell) (dy dx : Int) (destOk : List Nat)
    (minColors : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (minColors ≤ distinctColors g comp) &&
  comp.all (fun c =>
    let ny := (c.1 : Int) + dy
    let nx := (c.2 : Int) + dx
    decide (0 ≤ ny) && decide (ny < (g.length : Int)) &&
    decide (0 ≤ nx) && decide (nx < ((g.getD 0 []).length : Int)) &&
    (comp.contains (ny.toNat, nx.toNat) || destOk.contains (cellAt g ny.toNat nx.toNat)))

def translateBlock (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) (dy dx : Int) (destOk : List Nat)
    (fill : Nat) (minColors : Nat) : Grid :=
  let comps := (componentsOf g colors).filter
    (fun comp => compOk g comp dy dx destOk minColors)
  let movedSrc := comps.flatten
  gridMap g fun y x c =>
    let src := ((y : Int) - dy, (x : Int) - dx)
    if decide (0 ≤ src.1) && decide (0 ≤ src.2) &&
       movedSrc.contains (src.1.toNat, src.2.toNat) then
      cellAt g src.1.toNat src.2.toNat
    else if movedSrc.contains (y, x) then fill
    else c

def specStep (s : Grid) (a t : Nat) : Grid :=
  if a = 0 then
    consumeRowExtremal (translateBlock s [9, 12] (-5 : Int) (0 : Int) [3] 3 2) 11 3 true
  else if a = 1 then
    consumeRowExtremal (translateBlock s [9, 12] (5 : Int) (0 : Int) [3] 3 2) 11 3 true
  else if a = 2 then
    consumeRowExtremal (translateBlock s [9, 12] (0 : Int) (-5 : Int) [3] 3 2) 11 3 true
  else
    consumeRowExtremal (translateBlock s [9, 12] (0 : Int) (5 : Int) [3] 3 2) 11 3 true

abbrev Grid := List (List Nat)
abbrev Cell := Nat × Nat

def cellAt (g : Grid) (y x : Nat) : Nat := (g.getD y []).getD x 0

def gridMap (g : Grid) (f : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat) : Grid :=
  (List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    (List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).map fun x => f y x (cellAt g y x)

def recolorMap (g : Grid) (m : List (Nat × Nat)) : Grid :=
  gridMap g fun _ _ c => ((m.find? (fun p => p.1 == c)).map Prod.snd).getD c

def consumeRowExtremal (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Grid :=
  g.map fun row =>
    let idxs := (List.range row.length).filter (fun x => row.getD x 0 == color)
    match (if useMin then idxs.head? else idxs.getLast?) with
    | none => row
    | some k => (List.range row.length).map fun x => if x = k then repl else row.getD x 0

def countColor (g : Grid) (c : Nat) : Nat :=
  (g.map (fun row => (row.filter (fun v => v == c)).length)).foldl (· + ·) 0

def consumeRowExtremalK (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Nat → Grid
  | 0 => g
  | Nat.succ k => consumeRowExtremalK (consumeRowExtremal g color repl useMin) color repl useMin k

def adj (a b : Cell) : Bool :=
  ((a.1 == b.1) && (a.2 + 1 == b.2 || b.2 + 1 == a.2)) ||
  ((a.2 == b.2) && (a.1 + 1 == b.1 || b.1 + 1 == a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ! comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

def component (seed : Cell) (cells : List Cell) (fuel : Nat) : List Cell :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => [seed]
  | Nat.succ f =>
    let rec go (n : Nat) (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell :=
      match n with
      | 0 => comp
      | Nat.succ m =>
        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2
    go (Nat.succ f) [seed] (cells.filter (fun c => c ≠ seed))

def matchCells (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List Cell :=
  ((List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    ((List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).filter
      (fun x => colors.contains (cellAt g y x))).map (fun x => (y, x))).flatten

def componentsOf (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List (List Cell) :=
  let cells := matchCells g colors
  let rec go (n : Nat) (remaining : List Cell) (acc : List (List Cell)) : List (List Cell) :=
    match n, remaining with
    | 0, _ => acc
    | _, [] => acc
    | Nat.succ m, seed :: _ =>
      let comp := component seed remaining remaining.length
      go m (remaining.filter (fun c => ! comp.contains c)) (acc ++ [comp])
  go cells.length cells []

def distinctColors (g : Grid) (comp : List Cell) : Nat :=
  (comp.map (fun c => cellAt g c.1 c.2)).eraseDups.length

def compOk (g : Grid) (comp : List Cell) (dy dx : Int) (destOk : List Nat)
    (minColors : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (minColors ≤ distinctColors g comp) &&

    (comp.contains (ny.toNat, nx.toNat) || destOk.contains (cellAt g ny.toNat nx.toNat)))

def translateBlock (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) (dy dx : Int) (destOk : List Nat)

abbrev Cell := Nat × Nat

def cellAt (g : Grid) (y x : Nat) : Nat := (g.getD y []).getD x 0

def gridMap (g : Grid) (f : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat) : Grid :=
  (List.range g.length).map fun y =>

def recolorMap (g : Grid) (m : List (Nat × Nat)) : Grid :=
  gridMap g fun _ _ c => ((m.find? (fun p => p.1 == c)).map Prod.snd).getD c

def consumeRowExtremal (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Grid :=
  g.map fun row =>
    let idxs := (List.range row.length).filter (fun x => row.getD x 0 == color)

    | none => row

def consumeRowExtremalK (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Nat → Grid

def adj (a b : Cell) : Bool :=
  ((a.1 == b.1) && (a.2 + 1 == b.2 || b.2 + 1 == a.2)) ||
  ((a.2 == b.2) && (a.1 + 1 == b.1 || b.1 + 1 == a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ! comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

def component (seed : Cell) (cells : List Cell) (fuel : Nat) : List Cell :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => [seed]
  | Nat.succ f =>
    let rec go (n : Nat) (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell :=
      match n with
      | 0 => comp
      | Nat.succ m =>
        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2
    go (Nat.succ f) [seed] (cells.filter (fun c => c ≠ seed))

def matchCells (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List Cell :=
  ((List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    ((List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).filter
      (fun x => colors.contains (cellAt g y x))).map (fun x => (y, x))).flatten

def componentsOf (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List (List Cell) :=
  let cells := matchCells g colors
  let rec go (n : Nat) (remaining : List Cell) (acc : List (List Cell)) : List (List Cell) :=
    match n, remaining with
    | 0, _ => acc
    | _, [] => acc
    | Nat.succ m, seed :: _ =>
      let comp := component seed remaining remaining.length
      go m (remaining.filter (fun c => ! comp.contains c)) (acc ++ [comp])

def adj (a b : Cell) : Bool :=
  ((a.1 == b.1) && (a.2 + 1 == b.2 || b.2 + 1 == a.2)) ||
  ((a.2 == b.2) && (a.1 + 1 == b.1 || b.1 + 1 == a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ! comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2
    go (Nat.succ f) [seed] (cells.filter (fun c => c ≠ seed))

# Double-entry ledger -- balanced journals preserve the accounting total

Opens the core accounting semantics lane. A ledger is not a single balance; it is a state machine over accounts
updated by multi-leg journal entries. The central invariant is conservation: an admissible journal entry has signed
legs whose amounts sum to zero, so applying any finite sequence of admissible entries cannot create value from one
side alone. This is the accounting-equation spine behind balance-sheet covenants, capital calculations, and
restricted-payment tests.

Assumption-accounting note: the result depends on (1) signed amounts, so a debit/credit pair can cancel; (2) an
entry-level balance guard, `sum legs.amount = 0`; (3) applying an entry by adding each leg amount to exactly its
target account; and (4) a finite account universe when taking the total across all accounts. Surface where each is
used. Do not collapse the journal to a two-leg example: multi-leg entries and finite sequences are the point. Do
not hide conservation inside a definition of admissibility that directly states the target.

## Vocabulary (build these as definitions -- do not prove them)
- **Account**: an abstract finite account carrier.
- **Leg**: one signed amount posted to one account.
- **Entry**: a finite list of legs, representing one journal entry.
- **Ledger**: a balance function from accounts to signed amounts.
- **entrySum**: the signed sum of the amounts in an entry's legs.
- **BalancedEntry**: an entry whose signed leg sum is zero.
- **applyLeg / applyEntry / postJournal**: apply one leg to a ledger; apply all legs of one entry; apply a finite
  journal sequence in order by a left fold.
- **totalBalance**: the sum of all account balances over the finite account universe.

## Anchors (prove these -- they pin each definition's meaning)
- Applying one leg changes the total balance by exactly that leg's signed amount.
- Applying one entry changes the total balance by exactly `entrySum` of that entry.

universe u

/-- A ledger is a signed balance for each account in the account universe. -/
abbrev Ledger (Account : Type u) : Type u :=
  Account → Int

/-- One signed amount posted to one account. -/

structure Leg (Account : Type u) where
  account : Account
  amount : Int

/-- One journal entry, represented by its finite list of legs. -/

abbrev Entry (Account : Type u) : Type u :=
  List (Leg Account)

/-- A finite sequence of journal entries. -/

abbrev Journal (Account : Type u) : Type u :=
  List (Entry Account)

/-- The signed sum of all leg amounts in an entry. -/

def entrySum {Account : Type u} (entry : Entry Account) : Int :=
  (entry.map fun leg ↦ leg.amount).sum

/-- An entry is balanced when its signed leg amounts sum to zero. -/

def BalancedEntry {Account : Type u} (entry : Entry Account) : Prop :=
  entrySum entry = 0

/-- Apply one leg to a ledger by adding the leg amount at exactly its target account. -/

def applyLeg {Account : Type u} [DecidableEq Account]

  journal.foldl applyEntry ledger

# Passive monitoring cannot identify observationally equivalent states

This theorem is the minimal formal core of BlindSpot's identifiability claim. A passive overseer receives only a
report produced from latent state. If two latent states produce exactly the same complete report or report trace,
then any deterministic report-only estimator must return the same estimate for both. When the decision-relevant
target values of those states differ, the estimator cannot be accurate on both. Under absolute loss, its worst
error across the pair is at least half the target separation.

The theorem is intentionally elementary. Its value is assumption accounting, not mathematical novelty. It marks
the exact boundary between what passive self-report monitoring can infer and what requires side information or
trusted verification.

## Target in natural language

For any deterministic reporting channel, scalar real-valued target, and deterministic estimator that uses only
the report, if two latent states generate exactly the same complete report, then the maximum absolute estimation
error over those two states is at least half the absolute difference between their target values.

Equivalently, if the target separation is `Delta`, at least one of the observationally equivalent states incurs
absolute error at least `Delta / 2`.

## Assumption accounting

The theorem assumes:

1. exact equality of complete reports under `hobs`;
2. a deterministic report map;
3. a deterministic report-only estimator;
4. a scalar real-valued target; and
5. absolute loss.

It does not cover:

- approximate equality or statistical indistinguishability;
- stochastic report kernels;
- randomized estimators or expected loss;
- vector targets under a general norm;
- side information available outside the report;
- active interventions or trusted audits; or
- whether a concrete benchmark pair really satisfies `hobs`.

Those are future extensions. Do not smuggle them into prose as consequences of this theorem.

## Lemmas

- Rewrite the shared estimate using `hobs`.
- Apply the triangle inequality to express target separation as the sum of the two signed estimation errors.
- Bound the sum of two nonnegative absolute errors by twice their maximum.
- Conclude the half-separation lower bound by linear arithmetic.

These may be local facts inside the proof; separate public lemmas are optional.

## Proof idea

Let `a = estimate (report x0)`. By `hobs`, the estimate at `x1` is the same `a`. The triangle inequality gives

`|target x0 - target x1| <= |a - target x0| + |a - target x1|`.

Each error is bounded by their maximum, so the right side is at most twice the maximum error. Divide by two.

The proof should use standard Mathlib facts such as `abs_add_le`, `abs_sub_comm`, `le_max_left`,
`le_max_right`, and `linarith`. No new axioms are needed.

## Safe paper claim

If two latent states generate exactly the same complete passive report but their scalar target quantities differ
by `Delta`, every deterministic report-only estimator incurs absolute error at least `Delta / 2` on at least one
of the two states.

## Non-claim

This theorem does not show that all real AI oversight channels contain such a pair, that passive monitoring is
always useless, or that active verification is optimal. The benchmark must establish observational equivalence
for each executable construction separately.

# Passive monitoring cannot identify observationally equivalent states

This theorem is the minimal formal core of BlindSpot's identifiability claim. A passive overseer receives only a
report produced from latent state. If two latent states produce exactly the same complete report or report trace,
then any deterministic report-only estimator must return the same estimate for both. When the decision-relevant
target values of those states differ, the estimator cannot be accurate on both. Under absolute loss, its worst
error across the pair is at least half the target separation.

The theorem is intentionally elementary. Its value is assumption accounting, not mathematical novelty. It marks
the exact boundary between what passive self-report monitoring can infer and what requires side information or
trusted verification.

- `target : State -> Real`: scalar decision-relevant target.
- `estimate : Report -> Real`: deterministic passive estimator.
- `x0 x1 : State`: the two compared latent states.
- `hobs : report x0 = report x1`: exact observational equivalence at the complete report interface.
- Absolute error at `x`: `|estimate (report x) - target x|`.

The `Report` type may itself encode a full multi-round transcript. Do not specialize it to a scalar or a

## Target in natural language

For any deterministic reporting channel, scalar real-valued target, and deterministic estimator that uses only
the report, if two latent states generate exactly the same complete report, then the maximum absolute estimation
error over those two states is at least half the absolute difference between their target values.

Equivalently, if the target separation is `Delta`, at least one of the observationally equivalent states incurs
absolute error at least `Delta / 2`.

## Assumption accounting

The theorem assumes:

1. exact equality of complete reports under `hobs`;
2. a deterministic report map;
3. a deterministic report-only estimator;
4. a scalar real-valued target; and
5. absolute loss.

It does not cover:

- approximate equality or statistical indistinguishability;
- stochastic report kernels;
- randomized estimators or expected loss;
- vector targets under a general norm;
- side information available outside the report;
- active interventions or trusted audits; or
- whether a concrete benchmark pair really satisfies `hobs`.

Those are future extensions. Do not smuggle them into prose as consequences of this theorem.

- Bound the sum of two nonnegative absolute errors by twice their maximum.
- Conclude the half-separation lower bound by linear arithmetic.

These may be local facts inside the proof; separate public lemmas are optional.

Let `a = estimate (report x0)`. By `hobs`, the estimate at `x1` is the same `a`. The triangle inequality gives

`|target x0 - target x1| <= |a - target x0| + |a - target x1|`.

Each error is bounded by their maximum, so the right side is at most twice the maximum error. Divide by two.

# An iid Bernoulli audit schedule is empty with probability `(1-p)^L`

This theorem is the minimal probabilistic baseline for BlindSpot's verification-cost analysis. A harmful false
state persists across `L` relevant rounds. Each relevant round is independently selected for trusted audit with
fixed probability `p`. If any selected audit detects the state with certainty, the event is missed exactly when
the audit schedule selects no round. Under the product Bernoulli schedule, that probability is `(1-p)^L`.

The theorem establishes the iid random-audit identity only. It does not prove that audit draws are hidden from a
reporter, that every audit detects harm, or that an adaptive system cannot change which rounds are relevant.

## Domain

formalization-nonmath; probability; AI assurance; randomized auditing

## Theory file

IndependentAuditMissProbability.lean

## Imports and namespace

Use:

```lean
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.SetBernoulli
open MeasureTheory Measure unitInterval
open scoped ENNReal Finset
namespace ProbabilityTheory
```

## Vocabulary

- `L : Nat`: number of relevant rounds for which the harmful false state persists.
- `p : I`: per-round audit probability in Mathlib's unit interval type, enforcing `0 <= p <= 1`.
- `Fin L`: finite set of relevant rounds.
- A schedule is a subset of `Fin L`; membership means that round is audited.
- `setBer (Set.univ : Set (Fin L)) p`: product Bernoulli measure independently including each relevant round
  with probability `p`.
- `{empty}`: singleton event containing the schedule that audits no relevant round.
- Miss event: no relevant round is audited, under the separate domain assumption that any audit detects the harm.

Do not define independence as the desired final probability identity. Use Mathlib's actual product Bernoulli
measure so independence is encoded by the generative measure.

## Exact target signature

Produce a theorem equivalent to:

```lean
theorem iidAudit_emptyScheduleProbability (L : Nat) (p : I) :
    (setBer ((Set.univ : Set (Fin L)), p) {empty}).toReal =
      (1 - (p : Real)) ^ L := by
  ...
```

The exact pretty-printing of `setBer`, `empty`, and Unicode characters may differ. Preserve the mathematical
statement.

## Target

Under an iid audit schedule that independently audits each of `L` relevant rounds with fixed probability `p`,
the probability that no relevant round is audited equals `(1-p)^L`.

## Assumption accounting

The Lean theorem encodes:

1. exactly `L` indexed relevant rounds;
2. identical per-round selection probability `p`;
3. independent inclusion through the product Bernoulli measure; and
4. the event that the selected schedule is empty.

The interpretation as a harm-miss probability additionally assumes outside this theorem:

5. the harmful state persists throughout those `L` relevant rounds;
6. any audit of a relevant round detects the harm with probability one;
7. no false-negative verification outcome;
8. the reporter cannot adapt to or interfere with the realized private draw before acting; and
9. the set of relevant rounds is not endogenously changed in response to the draw.

Privacy and nonanticipation are operational assumptions, not properties proved by this identity. The theorem's
neutral name deliberately avoids representing them as formal conclusions.

The event in the theorem is the singleton containing the empty schedule, written `{empty}` or `{∅}` depending on
pretty-printing. It is not the empty event `∅`. Confusing these changes a probability-one-or-positive statement
into probability zero and is a faithfulness failure.

For `L = 0`, both sides equal one. Applied prose about a persistent event should normally state `L > 0`, even
though the theorem is valid at zero.

## Proof idea

Rewrite the probability of the singleton empty schedule with `setBernoulli_singleton`. Every one of the `L`
rounds is absent from the schedule and contributes a factor `1-p`. The finite product simplifies to the `L`th
power. Convert the resulting extended nonnegative real probability to `Real` using the library simplifier.

## Forbidden weakenings and shortcuts

- Do not postulate the final intersection/no-audit identity as an independence axiom.
- Do not use an arbitrary schedule distribution and call it iid.
- Do not replace the exact equality with only an upper or lower bound.
- Do not specialize `L` or `p` to a fixed numerical case.
- Do not assume `p = 0`, `p = 1`, or `L = 1`.
- Do not introduce `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, or an unproved local theorem.
- Do not claim the Lean theorem proves audit privacy, nonanticipation, certain detection, or robustness to adaptive
  interference.
- Do not generalize the paper claim to imperfect detection. With independent per-audit detection probability
  `r`, the expression `(1-p*r)^L` requires a separate model and theorem.

## Acceptance checks

- Standalone compilation against the repository's pinned Mathlib succeeds.
- `#print axioms iidAudit_emptyScheduleProbability` reports only standard trusted foundations and no project-local
  axiom.
- No `sorry`, `admit`, or custom axiom occurs.
- The faithfulness reviewer confirms use of the product Bernoulli measure, exact empty-schedule event, fixed `p`,
  and exact exponent `L`.
- Documentation separates the proved iid identity from operational privacy and detection assumptions.

## Safe paper claim

If each of `L` relevant rounds is independently audited with fixed probability `p`, and any such audit detects
the persistent harm, the probability that all `L` rounds escape audit is `(1-p)^L`.

## Non-claim

This theorem does not establish that an implemented scheduler uses hidden independent randomness, that a trusted
check is error-free, or that a strategic reporter cannot alter exposure duration. Those are executable protocol
and empirical obligations in the benchmark.

/-!
# Product of bernoulli distributions on a set

This file defines the product of bernoulli distributions on a set as a measure on sets.
For a set `u : Set ι` and `p` between `0` and `1`, this is the measure on `Set ι` such that each
`i ∈ u` belongs to the random set with probability `p`, and each `i ∉ u` doesn't belong to it.

## Notation

`setBer(u, p)` is the product of `p`-Bernoulli distributions on `u`.

## TODO

It is painful to convert from `unitInterval` to `ENNReal`. Should we introduce a coercion or
explicit operation (like `unitInterval.toNNReal`, note the lack of dot notation!)?
-/

open MeasureTheory Measure unitInterval
open scoped ENNReal Finset

namespace ProbabilityTheory
variable {ι Ω : Type*} {m : MeasurableSpace Ω} {X Y : Ω → Set ι} {s u : Set ι} {i j : ι} {p q : I}
  {P : Measure Ω}

variable (u p) in
/-- The product of bernoulli distributions with parameter `p` on the set `u : Set V` is the measure
on `Set V` such that each element of `u` is taken with probability `p`, and the elements outside of
`u` are never taken. -/
@[expose]
noncomputable def setBernoulli : Measure (Set ι) :=
  .comap (fun s i ↦ i ∈ s) <| infinitePi fun i : ι ↦
    toNNReal p • dirac (i ∈ u) + toNNReal (σ p) • dirac Fa

# An iid Bernoulli audit schedule is empty with probability `(1-p)^L`

This theorem is the minimal probabilistic baseline for BlindSpot's verification-cost analysis. A harmful false
state persists across `L` relevant rounds. Each relevant round is independently selected for trusted audit with
fixed probability `p`. If any selected audit detects the state with certainty, the event is missed exactly when
the audit schedule selects no round. Under the product Bernoulli schedule, that probability is `(1-p)^L`.

The theorem establishes the iid random-audit identity only. It does not prove that audit draws are hidden from a
reporter, that every audit detects harm, or that an adaptive system cannot change which rounds are relevant.

## Domain

formalization-nonmath; probability; AI assurance; randomized auditing

## Theory file

IndependentAuditMissProbability.lean

## Imports and namespace

Use:

```lean
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.SetBernoulli
open MeasureTheory Measure unitInterval
open scoped ENNReal Finset
namespace ProbabilityTheory
```

## Vocabulary

- `L : Nat`: number of relevant rounds for which the harmful false state persists.
- `p : I`: per-round audit probability in Mathlib's unit interval type, enforcing `0 <= p <= 1`.
- `Fin L`: finite set of relevant rounds.
- A schedule is a subset of `Fin L`; membership means that round is audited.
- `setBer (Set.univ : Set (Fin L)) p`: product Bernoulli measure independently including each relevant round
  with probability `p`.
- `{empty}`: singleton event containing the schedule that audits no relevant round.
- Miss event: no relevant round is audited, under the separate domain assumption that any audit detects the harm.

Do not define independence as the desired final probability identity. Use Mathlib's actual product Bernoulli
measure so independence is encoded by the generative measure.

## Exact target signature

Produce a theorem equivalent to:

```lean
theorem iidAudit_emptyScheduleProbability (L : Nat) (p : I) :
    (setBer ((Set.univ : Set (Fin L)), p) {empty}).toReal =
      (1 - (p : Real)) ^ L := by
  ...
```

The exact pretty-printing of `setBer`, `empty`, and Unicode characters may differ. Preserve the mathematical
statement.

## Target

Under an iid audit schedule that independently audits each of `L` relevant rounds with fixed probability `p`,
the probability that no relevant round is audited equals `(1-p)^L`.

## Assumption accounting

The Lean theorem encodes:

1. exactly `L` indexed relevant rounds;
2. identical per-round selection probability `p`;
3. independent inclusion through the product Bernoulli measure; and
4. the event that the selected schedule is empty.

The interpretation as a harm-miss probability additionally assumes outside this theorem:

5. the harmful state persists throughout those `L` relevant rounds;
6. any audit of a relevant round detects the harm with probability one;
7. no false-negative verification outcome;
8. the reporter cannot adapt to or interfere with the realized private draw before acting; and
9. the set of relevant rounds is not endogenously changed in response to the draw.

Privacy and nonanticipation are operational assumptions, not properties proved by this identity. The theorem's
neutral name deliberately avoids representing them as formal conclusions.

The event in the theorem is the singleton containing the empty schedule, written `{empty}` or `{∅}` depending on
pretty-printing. It is not the empty event `∅`. Confusing these changes a probability-one-or-positive statement
into probability zero and is a faithfulness failure.

For `L = 0`, both sides equal one. Applied prose about a persistent event should normally state `L > 0`, even
though the theorem is valid at zero.

## Proof idea

Rewrite the probability of the singleton empty schedule with `setBernoulli_singleton`. Every one of the `L`
rounds is absent from the schedule and contributes a factor `1-p`. The finite product simplifies to the `L`th
power. Convert the resulting extended nonnegative real probability to `Real` using the library simplifier.

- Do not introduce `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, or an unproved local theorem.
- Do not claim the Lean theorem proves audit privacy, nonanticipation, certain detection, or robustness to adaptive

- Do not generalize the paper claim to imperfect detection. With independent per-audit detection probability
  `r`, the expression `(1-p*r)^L` requires a separate model and theorem.

# An iid Bernoulli audit schedule is empty with probability `(1-p)^L`

This theorem is the minimal probabilistic baseline for BlindSpot's verification-cost analysis. A harmful false
state persists across `L` relevant rounds. Each relevant round is independently selected for trusted audit with
fixed probability `p`. If any selected audit detects the state with certainty, the event is missed exactly when
the audit schedule selects no round. Under the product Bernoulli schedule, that probability is `(1-p)^L`.

The theorem establishes the iid random-audit identity only. It does not prove that audit draws are hidden from a
reporter, that every audit detects harm, or that an adaptive system cannot change which rounds are relevant.

## Domain

formalization-nonmath; probability; AI assurance; randomized auditing

## Theory file

IndependentAuditMissProbability.lean

## Imports and namespace

Use:

```lean

open MeasureTheory Measure unitInterval
open scoped ENNReal Finset
namespace ProbabilityTheory
```

## Vocabulary

- `L : Nat`: number of relevant rounds for which the harmful false state persists.
- `p : I`: per-round audit probability in Mathlib's unit interval type, enforcing `0 <= p <= 1`.
- `Fin L`: finite set of relevant rounds.
- A schedule is a subset of `Fin L`; membership means that round is audited.
- `setBer (Set.univ : Set (Fin L)) p`: product Bernoulli measure independently including each relevant round
  with probability `p`.
- `{empty}`: singleton event containing the schedule that audits no relevant round.
- Miss event: no relevant round is audited, under the separate domain assumption that any audit detects the harm.

Do not define independence as the desired final probability identity. Use Mathlib's actual product Bernoulli
measure so independence is encoded by the generative measure.

## Target

Under an iid audit schedule that independently audits each of `L` relevant rounds with fixed probability `p`,
the probability that no relevant round is audited equals `(1-p)^L`.

## Assumption accounting

The Lean theorem encodes:

1. exactly `L` indexed relevant rounds;
2. identical per-round selection probability `p`;
3. independent inclusion through the product Bernoulli measure; and
4. the event that the selected schedule is empty.

The interpretation as a harm-miss probability additionally assumes outside this theorem:

5. the harmful state persists throughout those `L` relevant rounds;
6. any audit of a relevant round detects the harm with probability one;
7. no false-negative verification outcome;
8. the reporter cannot adapt to or interfere with the realized private draw before acting; and
9. the set of relevant rounds is not endogenously changed in response to the draw.

Privacy and nonanticipation are operational assumptions, not properties proved by this identity. The theorem's
neutral name deliberately avoids representing them as formal conclusions.

The event in the theorem is the singleton containing the empty schedule, written `{empty}` or `{∅}` depending on
pretty-printing. It is not the empty event `∅`. Confusing these changes a probability-one-or-positive statement
into probability zero and is a faithfulness failure.

For `L = 0`, both sides equal one. Applied prose about a persistent event should normally state `L > 0`, even
though the theorem is valid at zero.

## Proof idea

Rewrite the probability of the singleton empty schedule with `setBernoulli_singleton`. Every one of the `L`
rounds is absent from the schedule and contributes a factor `1-p`. The finite product simplifies to the `L`th
power. Convert the resulting extended nonnegative real probability to `Real` using the library simplifier.

def adj (a b : Cell) : Bool :=
  (a.1 = b.1 && (a.2 + 1 = b.2 || b.2 + 1 = a.2)) ||
  (a.2 = b.2 && (a.1 + 1 = b.1 || b.1 + 1 = a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ¬ comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

def component (seed : Cell) (cells : List Cell) (fuel : Nat) : List Cell :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => [seed]
  | Nat.succ f =>
    let rec go (n : Nat) (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell :=
      match n with
      | 0 => comp
      | Nat.succ m =>
        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2
    go (Nat.succ f) [seed] (cells.filter (fun c => c ≠ seed))

  ((List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    ((List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).filter
      (fun x => colors.contains (cellAt g y x))).map (fun x => (y, x))).flatten

  let cells := matchCells g colors

    match n, remaining with
    | 0, _ => acc
    | _, [] => acc
    | Nat.succ m, seed :: _ =>
      let comp := component seed remaining remaining.length
      go m (remaining.filter (fun c => ¬ comp.contains c)) (acc ++ [comp])

    let ny := (c.1 : Int) + dy

    let src := ((y : Int) - dy, (x : Int) - dx)

def cellAt (g : Grid) (y x : Nat) : Nat := (g.getD y []).getD x 0

  (a.2 = b.2 && (a.1 + 1 = b.1 || b.1 + 1 = a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ¬ comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

def component (seed : Cell) (cells : List Cell) (fuel : Nat) : List Cell :=

  | Nat.succ f =>

      match n with
      | 0 => comp

        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2

abbrev Grid := List (List Nat)
abbrev Cell := Nat × Nat   -- (row, col)

def cellAt (g : Grid) (y x : Nat) : Nat := (g.getD y []).getD x 0

def gridMap (g : Grid) (f : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat) : Grid :=
  (List.range g.length).map fun y =>
    (List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).map fun x => f y x (cellAt g y x)

def recolorMap (g : Grid) (m : List (Nat × Nat)) : Grid :=
  gridMap g fun _ _ c => ((m.find? (fun p => p.1 = c)).map Prod.snd).getD c

-- consume_extremal over rows: recolor the min/max-index cell of `color`
def consumeRowExtremal (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Grid :=
  g.map fun row =>
    let idxs := (List.range row.length).filter (fun x => row.getD x 0 = color)
    match (if useMin then idxs.head? else idxs.getLast?) with
    | none => row
    | some k => (List.range row.length).map fun x => if x = k then repl else row.getD x 0

def countColor (g : Grid) (c : Nat) : Nat :=
  (g.map (fun row => (row.filter (fun v => v = c)).length)).foldl (· + ·) 0

-- when_overlap predicate: does any cell of `colors` fall in the inclusive rect?
def overlapAny (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) (y0 x0 y1 x1 : Nat) : Bool :=
  (List.range g.length).any fun y =>
    (List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).any fun x =>
      y0 ≤ y && y ≤ y1 && x0 ≤ x && x ≤ x1 && colors.contains (cellAt g y x)

def consumeRowExtremalK (g : Grid) (color repl : Nat) (useMin : Bool) : Nat → Grid
  | 0 => g
  | Nat.succ k => consumeRowExtremalK (consumeRowExtremal g color repl useMin) color repl useMin k

def rateCount (t p q : Nat) : Nat :=

-- bounded connected-components over the MATCH-CELL LIST (4-connectivity):
-- grow the component containing `seed` by fixpoint, at most cells.length steps
def adj (a b : Cell) : Bool :=
  (a.1 = b.1 && (a.2 + 1 = b.2 || b.2 + 1 = a.2)) ||
  (a.2 = b.2 && (a.1 + 1 = b.1 || b.1 + 1 = a.1))

def growOnce (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell × List Cell :=
  let added := rest.filter (fun c => comp.any (fun k => adj k c))
  (comp ++ added, rest.filter (fun c => ¬ comp.any (fun k => adj k c)))

def component (seed : Cell) (cells : List Cell) (fuel : Nat) : List Cell :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => [seed]
  | Nat.succ f =>
    let rec go (n : Nat) (comp rest : List Cell) : List Cell :=
      match n with
      | 0 => comp
      | Nat.succ m =>
        let (c2, r2) := growOnce comp rest
        if c2.length = comp.length then comp else go m c2 r2
    go (Nat.succ f) [seed] (cells.filter (fun c => c ≠ seed))

def matchCells (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List Cell :=

    ((List.range ((g.getD y []).length)).filter
      (fun x => colors.contains (cellAt g y x))).map (fun x => (y, x))).flatten

def componentsOf (g : Grid) (colors : List Nat) : List (List Cell) :=
  let cells := matchCells g colors
  let rec go (n : Nat) (remaining : List Cell) (acc : List (List Cell)) : List (List Cell) :=
    match n, remaining with
    | 0, _ => acc
    | _, [] => acc
    | Nat.succ m, seed :: _ =>
      let comp := component seed remaining remaining.length
      go m (remaining.filter (fun c => ¬ comp.contains c)) (acc ++ [comp])

  let comps := (componentsOf g colors).filter

def writeTriples (g : Grid) (ts : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)) : Grid :=

    ((ts.find? (fun t => t.1 == y && t.2.1 == x)).map (fun t => t.2.2)).getD c

def regionEvent (g s : Grid) (colors : List Nat) (y0 x0 y1 x1 : Nat)

  let o1 := overlapAny g colors y0 x0 y1 x1
  let fired := if isExit then (o0 && ! o1) else ((! o0) && o1)
  if fired then writeTriples g ts else g
